findings.title: Exact email lookup lets casing changes bypass the blocklist
findings.body: This lookup compares the submitted address verbatim with the stored address, and signup does not normalize the email before validation. Because email domains are case-insensitive, a user can submit the same address with different domain casing (for example, `bad@SPAMCLUB.COM` instead of `bad@spamclub.com`) and avoid the blocklist match. Normalize both stored and submitted addresses before comparing them.

findings.title: Validation side effects count each signup attempt more than once
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments match statistics, but it is called from a validator, which can run multiple times for one operation. In particular, `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again; a matching address therefore increments `match_count` twice for one signup attempt. Keep validation side-effect-free and record a match once at the submission boundary.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose counter increments
findings.body: The counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two signup validations load the same row before either saves, both can write the same incremented value, losing one match from `match_count`. Use an atomic database increment (and update the timestamp atomically) or lock the row.
